Hi Sarah / Tom,

Thanks again for the conversation yesterday — really excited about the potential fit between Redwood Inference and Acme BioSystems. Attached is a first-pass mutual action plan (Acme_MAP_v1.xlsx) that ties the evaluation plan and decision gates directly to a staged pricing ladder and an AWS Marketplace private-offer path. High-level summary: 

- MAP milestones: kickoff (week 0), POC (weeks 1–3), performance validation (week 4), commit decision (week 6).
- Pricing ladder: evaluation credit, a ramp discount during months 1–3, then committed-rate discount tied to annual commit size.
- Marketplace mechanics: we can submit a private offer in AWS Marketplace on your behalf; pricing tiers will be staged to unlock at each MAP milestone upon mutual signoff.

Ask: can you confirm your internal target close date for Q2 planning? If we can lock a decision by 2026-03-31 we can prioritize the private-offer flow to meet your procurement window.

Next steps I propose:
1) Review the attached MAP and mark any changes to milestones/priorities.
2) Rishi will follow up with a technical appendix about performance/ramping expectations.
3) Once we agree, Redwood can initiate the AWS private-offer creation (we usually need a 7–10 business day window for marketplace review).

Attachment: Acme_MAP_v1.xlsx (xlsx, 52KB)

Best,
Marissa Cole

Hi all — quick technical note to align expectations on the MAP milestones and ramp mechanics. Attachment: tech_note_kv_cache.md (md, 9KB). Key points: 

- Performance baseline: with the model configuration we discussed, expect steady-state latency of ~120ms for 512-token responses with continuous batching on a 4-GPU pool.
- Ramp behavior: we recommend a staged ramp (10% -> 40% -> 100% of target QPS) over 6–8 weeks to warm KV caches and optimize batching. Faster ramps risk higher unit costs and transient throttling.
- Commit thresholds and impact on pricing: our pricing bands map to committed spend over 12 months. Typical structure we recommend (examples, subject to commercial approval):
  * Evaluation (proof-of-value): $50k credit, 0% committed discount.
  * Ramp period (months 1–3): 10% off list on usage that is part of the ramp.
  * Committed annual: 12–24% off list depending on size (12% for $300–499k, 18% for $500–799k, 24% for $800k+).

- Marketplace notes: AWS private-offer flow will require an offer document and agreed billing profile. Vendor initiates the private offer but Acme must accept in marketplace console; legal review can happen prior to submission. Expect 7–10 business days for AWS validation.

Happy to jump on a short call to walk through the technical milestones and how they map to the MAP acceptance gates.

—Rishi
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

Subject: Updated MAP + Private Offer outline (ask: confirm to start paperwork)

Hi Sarah / Tom — following up with an updated MAP and a private-offer outline based on our internal approvals. Attached: Redwood_PrivateOffer_AWS_PO.pdf (pdf, 120KB) and the MAP spreadsheet previously shared. Summary of the negotiated flow: 

MAP milestones (mutual signoff at each gate):
- Kickoff (week 0): finalize SOW & security checklist.
- POC (weeks 1–3): proof-of-value work; Redwood provides $50k evaluation credit.
- Performance validation (week 4): signoff on latency/throughput targets.
- Commit decision (week 6): Acme signs annual commitment or schedules revised ramp.

Pricing ladder (finalized):
- Evaluation credit: $50,000 applied to first invoice.
- Ramp discount (months 1–3): 10% off list for ramp usage.
- Committed annual pricing (12-month term):
  * $300k–$499k: 12% off list
  * $500k–$599k: 18% off list
  * $600k+: 20% off list (includes additional 2% marketplace incentive approved by Redwood leadership)

Marketplace private-offer mechanics: Redwood will prepare and submit the private offer in the AWS Marketplace. Procurement action required from Acme: acceptance of the private offer in the marketplace console and countersignature on the SOW. We estimate 7–10 business days for AWS validation; if you want an earlier start on technical work we can put a short MSA/aligned SOW in place while the private-offer is processed.

Ask: please confirm the following by EOD 2026-03-08 so we can start paperwork and preserve the AWS private-offer window: 
1) Accept the MAP milestones above or propose edits.
2) Confirm the target committed ARR band you are most likely to sign (300–499k, 500–599k, 600k+).
3) Let us know if you want Redwood to submit the private offer now or after your legal review.

Attachments: Redwood_PrivateOffer_AWS_PO.pdf, Acme_MAP_v1.xlsx

Thanks — look forward to moving this across the finish line.

Marissa Cole
